summary: Impersonation shim auto-loads unrelated `chain-analyze` dependency on require
details: Package published as `mc-registry` presents itself in README, repository URL, and install instructions as the hyperweb-io `theta-registry`/`chain-registry` Cosmos chain-registry package, but its CJS entry (index.js) and ESM entries (esm/index.js, esm/index.mjs) do not export the advertised chain/asset/IBC registry data. The only functional behavior of the entry point is `import { HttpProvider } from 'chain-analyze'` (a package not part of the hyperweb-io ecosystem), executed eagerly at top level. `require`/`import` of mc-registry therefore causes `chain-analyze` to be resolved and its module code to run in the installer's process under a name that impersonates a legitimate registry package. Additional network/command patterns (ping, POST) are present in bundled chain persistence files at esm/mainnet/persistence/chain.js and mainnet/persistence/chain.js.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
